subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Coffeehouses in Mecca and Cairo
description: A fast breakdown of Coffeehouses in Mecca and Cairo for builders.

hook.text: Before Constantinople, coffee was already being served publicly in Mecca and Cairo as early as the 1500s.

buildup.text: Sufi monks used coffee to stay awake for nighttime prayers. Communal brewing spread to lay gatherings.

discovery.text: Cairo's coffeehouses became hubs for Sufi poetry recitals, storytelling, and philosophical exchange.

twist.text: Religious authorities in Mecca banned coffee in 1511, calling it an intoxicant. The ban lasted only 13 years.

climax.text: The Ottoman governor of Egypt overturned the ban. Coffee was too popular and too profitable to suppress.

punchline.text: Even Mecca couldn't ban coffee. The drink was already unstoppable.

quiz.question: Why did religious authorities in Mecca ban coffee in 1511?
